definition: A newer generation of optimizers (Muon, Shampoo/SOAP lineage) that orthogonalize or precondition updates for matrix parameters, showing meaningful compute savings over AdamW in large-model training and adopted in several frontier-scale runs.
details: A newer generation of optimizers (Muon, Shampoo/SOAP lineage) that orthogonalize or precondition updates for matrix parameters, showing meaningful compute savings over AdamW in large-model training and adopted in several frontier-scale runs.

explainer.lead: Muon and second-order-flavored optimizers (Shampoo/SOAP lineage) orthogonalize or precondition updates for matrix parameters, showing meaningful compute savings over AdamW in large-model training. They matter because several frontier-scale training runs have adopted them.

tiers.eli5: Instead of nudging every knob the same way, these methods reorganize the update so training gets more done per step.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers swap them in for AdamW when training large models with matrix-valued parameters, aiming for compute savings. A pitfall is that reported gains come from large-scale runs, so benefits depend on the setting.
tiers.paperLevel: These optimizers orthogonalize or precondition updates for matrix parameters; against AdamW they have shown meaningful compute savings in large-model training and have been adopted in several frontier-scale runs.

explainer.example: A large-model training run uses Muon instead of AdamW for its matrix parameters, achieving meaningful compute savings over the AdamW baseline.
